lines.en: When I was younger, I watched a woman’s head split open after a collision with the concrete.
I was clutching my mother’s hand as if it were a life raft and I was lost in the ocean.
She pulled me inside to shield me from learning about death long before I was meant to.
In hindsight, I wish she wouldn’t have.
It happened outside of the grocery store.
We kept on shopping, ignoring the blare of the sirens — so loud that they overtook the music on the store radio and became the soundtrack to our trip for the day.
There is one moment I can recall where the sirens perfectly aligned with the tune of a song.
Like a parallelogram, they combined and stretched out forever — past the dying woman and deep into the street...
Off into the horizon...leaving a wake of intangible destruction as it went.
I followed the lines until their very end, but only in my mind as my hand still rested in that of my mother’s and I wasn’t old enough to wander off on my own yet.
I understand why now.
For when the lines ended, I was met with nothing more than pitch black.
And a single white clock, dissolving into nothingness.
I look down while I’m walking now.
Just to make sure no lines cross over me.
I recall another hand, far bigger than that of my mother’s.
With a large, clock-colored eraser pressed between its thumb and its forefinger, it reached off into the distance and started rubbing away the remnants of an unreadily dispatched soul.
But each line it erased only became longer at the end without attention.
And each fleck of rubber that peeled and fell off of the eraser while it attempted to fulfill its only purpose was replaced with a sprouting sunflower.
It was in that moment that it dawned on me.
The idea that the most beautiful of things can still grow in the shadows of all that is evil.
And it is for that reason that I call myself what I do today.
For that hand was yours.
And that flower was me.
: Uhh...Makoto?
: What?
: There’s someone here to see you.
: Sorry, but I’m not accepting any visitors right now. Please ask whoever it is to go away.
: Even if it’s me?
: It doesn’t make a difference who you are. I said I’m not accepting visitors.
: Well, I tried.
: Did you really, though?
: Tried?
: Tried what?
: Did you think bringing him here would cheer me up?
: Do you think I’m an inconvenience because I’m not handling this as well as you? Is that what’s going on here?
: What? Of course not. You’re not an inconvenience at all. I just hate seeing you like-
: Get out.
: Makoto, please. I brought him all this way here to-
: Not him. You. Leave.
: You shouldn’t talk to your mother like that.
: Oh? Are you my dad now? Hooray. Everything is good again.
: Let’s all hold hands and forget that the last one is never coming back.
: I get that you’re upset. But you need to apologize to-
: It’s fine, really.  You don’t have to worry about it.
: I kind of figured something like this was going to happen anyway.
: Hey, now. What’s that supposed to mean?
: Have I become so predictably horrible as a daughter that you just expect me to turn you away now?
: Or do you think that maybe I’d just have an easier time grieving without being reminded every thirty seconds that my father is dead?
: You know that’s not-
: Why are you still here? I asked you to leave.
: I’ll humor you and let Sensei try to “snap me out of this.” But if I were in your shoes, I’d probably use that time to prepare myself because, chances are, your daughter’s never coming back either.
: That’s not true...
: You’re still you...and all of this is just temporary.
: Oh, give me a fucking break with the cliche consolation lines like “all of this is temporary” and “things will get better.”
: At least Sensei will be able to come up with more creative ways to remind me of why I shouldn’t be crying during the saddest day of my life. Right, Sensei?
: Makoto! You’re not the only one who lost someone, you know?! He meant just as much to me as he did to you!
: Yeah? That’s good to know. It was hard to keep track of who meant what to who with all of those extra people always coming in and out of the house.
: That...didn’t have anything to do with-
: Yeah, yeah, yeah. Explain it later. I’m done dealing with you for now. Bring on the next contestant.
: Do you intend to shit talk me as well when I’m also here to help you?
: You’re here because you were fucking kidnapped, weren’t you? This isn’t something you would plan.
: You’d tell me to get the fuck over it and learn how to deal with things on my own because that’s what I’m supposed to do! Isn’t it?!
: No. That’s-
: Isn’t it?!?!
: ...As I was trying to say, no. This is different from all of those other times. Different enough that I’ve had a hard time thinking of anything but this since I walked into that bathroom.
: Oh, good! If all it took was a fucking death for you to start worrying about me, perhaps I should have killed someone myself!
: That’s not what he’s saying, Makoto!
: Why are you still here?! I told you to leave!
: I’ll take it from here, Maki. I remember the way out, so I can just come meet you in the shop when I’m done.
: Good. She was starting to test my patience anyway.
: Hallelujah! Praise fucking be!
: I just want you to feel better, Makoto.
: I’m sorry if I went about it the wrong way.
Maki leaves the room, exhibiting a surprising amount of self control by not slamming the door on her way out.
I understand that we all have our own ways of processing grief...and I understand even better just how much Makoto cared for her father.
But even then, I can’t help but feel like she’s being extremely unfair to a woman who’s been bending over backwards and sidelining her own grief just to deal with this.
If I were a parent in this scenario, I’d simply let my child rot.
So I guess it’s good that I’m not.
And that I won’t ever be.
Because it wouldn’t be fair to subject someone to that.
Now, please excuse me as my hypocrisy reigns supreme once more.
: Does being a bitch to your mother like that really make you feel any better?
: A little bit, yeah.
: Why? You do realize she’s taking this just as badly as you are, right?
: Dressed like that? Yeah, I don’t think so. You needn’t look any further than the clothes we’re wearing to tell she doesn’t give a shit.
: Wanna know what I really think, Sensei?
: I think she’s dressed like that because she wants somebody to fuck her so hard that she just forgets my dad.
: Seriously?
: What? It wouldn’t be the first time I’ve heard her getting her brains screwed out by some random guy.
: Want a shot? She’s fresh on the market. And her clothes are already halfway off. Saves you some of the hassle.
: Sounds good, actually. I’m sure that hearing me go to town on your mother while you’re stuck inside of your room will do plenty of good for your current state of mind.
: But what about your state of mind, Sensei? What if you’re not able to get it up for someone who’s already done growing?
: Oh well. Whatever. Just don’t come crying back to me when her insides are a little too “beat up” for you.
: I can’t speak from experience since you’re the only man who’s ever put his dick in me, but I’m pretty sure she might be a little too stretched out to appeal to your...tastes by now.
: Okay...can I sit? And can we talk about something that doesn’t involve sex?
: Wow! If I hadn’t already picked out my funeral dress, I might have thought it was my birthday after hearing that.
: Welcome to the party, Sensei. The seat at the head of the table is free now.
: My legs have grown since my dad last sat in it. So if we’re careful, I might even be able to give you a stealthy footjob while my mom tricks herself into believing we’re a big, happy family again.
: Would you rather I just leave?
: Do you want the honest answer to that? Or do you want to sit down regardless of what I want because it makes you feel better about yourself?
: I’ll sit. Thanks.
: Ooooh, look at you. Breezing right past my subtle digs at your character like they don’t actually hurt. Sure wish I could do that.
I take a seat beside Makoto, expecting her to slide away, but she doesn’t move at all.
In fact, she grows silent the second I’m closer to her- locking her hostility inside of a box, as temporary as it may be.
As I look down at her, I wonder if the disparity in size between us is the primary reason for her newfound silence.
I wonder if she feels safer now that there’s someone who could envelop her entire body in a single embrace just one foot away.
I wonder if that type of embrace is something she longs for in this moment.
Or if it would send her spiraling even further into a pit that she will never return from.
: Do you want to talk? Or would you rather sit here in silence?
: I’m not sure. I’m new to this whole “dead dad” thing.
: I see that, at the very least, you get your sense of humor from your mother. She said something eerily similar yesterday morning.
: Wow, it’s almost like we’re related or something.
: You don’t actually dislike her, do you?
: What do you think about her, Sensei? You know, since you two are such close friends now.
: I like her a lot, actually. She reminds me of this one girl that’s been following me around like a puppy since the school year began.
: Ami, because of how annoying she is? Ayane, because it seems as if she’s always in heat?
: I’m talking about you, obviously.
: And, for the record, you are also very annoying and have a surprisingly high sex drive.
: Yeah well, when you grow up surrounded by rubber cocks and screams of pleasure, you tend to find yourself getting interested in certain things at a very unhealthy age.
: Apart from that, though, my mother and I are nothing alike. We never have been.
: Well...spend a little more time focusing on her rather than everything else and maybe you’ll change your mind.
: Did she pay you to say that? Is that part of your mission today?
: If she did pay me to say that, you two would be even more alike. Because I distinctly recall you paying Miku on at least one occasion to...try to get me to fall for you or something.
: A decision that very well paid off in the fact that my hymen is now just as present as my father.
: If you really think that had any bearing on my decision to ultimately sleep with you, I think there’s a lot you don’t understand about this relationship.
: Well, it’s not as if you make it easy to understand.
: But, for the purpose of both humoring you and finding humor of my own, please tell me exactly what you think I have in common with my mother.
: Because apart from our apparent shared sex drive and our looks, I struggle finding anything at all.
: Well, there’s the dark sense of humor you both use to try and push some of the sadness away...
: There’s the overabundance of love you both have for Miku...
: But more than just those, there’s this...compulsion you both have to never look weak.
: Maki doesn’t look as fine as she does because she’s immune to this. She looks that way because she’s focusing everything she has on you right now.
: Weren’t you crying together when I walked into that bathroom?
: How should I know? I can’t remember anything about the day I found out. And all I remember from the day after is crying so hard that I threw up.
: Well, she was. And before that, she burst into the classroom searching for you with a look I have never seen from her before.
: It wasn’t sadness, either. It was urgency. Like the only thing that mattered in that moment was finding you so you wouldn’t have to hear the news from some staff member in an office.
: Everything after that has been a marathon of unrestrained compassion for a daughter that she loves who can’t even find it in her to return that love right now.

: Now, as one more person carrying the impossible, ingrained burden of never showing how I really feel, I obviously get that there’s a good reason for it. Which is why I’m not suggesting that you change that part of you.
: I just think you’re smarter than actually believing your mom is completely unaffected by this.
: Maybe I am.
: Maybe I am smart enough to understand that...
: But isn’t everything so much easier when you have someone else to blame?
: Isn’t it great knowing that the weight on your shoulders can just be passed on to someone else?! That burdens can become lighter whenever we want them to?!
: It’s not whenever we want. It’s whenever we can find someone willing to take that weight.
: And in your case, you’re just lucky that you have someone who’d sacrifice the last bit of sanity in them so you can be one step closer to smiling.
: Lucky...
: Me...lucky...
: Me...the girl who just lost her one and only hero...
: I’m lucky...
: I’m so lucky...
: Okay...lucky definitely wasn’t the best word choice on my part. But I’m sure you understand what I mean, don’t you?
: Of course I understand, Sensei.
: I’m smart...remember?
: Though, I suppose I’m not the smartest anymore.
: But I wouldn’t be that smart if I wasn’t trying to impress someone.
: And before you go drowning yourself in narcissism again, allow me to clarify that I’m not talking about you.
: The reason I worked so hard all those years...why I nearly KILLED MYSELF trying to become the best person I could be...
: It was all for him.
: It was all to make him proud.
: How am I gonna do that now?
: How am I supposed to keep being the best person I can be when the one thing making me that person isn’t here anymore?
: I’ve got nothing left.
: And don’t tell me I have you...or my mom...because you don’t love me...and she didn’t either until she had to.
: My dad is dead. The one thing keeping me going is dead.
: Shouldn’t I just die too?
: Maybe then, my mom wouldn’t have to hold in her tears. And you could have Nodoka become your new assistant since she’s already better than me.
: It would all be better without me. The whole fucking world.
: I’m nothing but a burden to everyone.
: There’s no one left that I want to live for.
: Then why not live for yourself?
: Because that’s fucking stupid.
: How? That’s what I do.
: Yeah? And how’s that working out for you?
: Fine, I guess.
: I’ve spent the last couple days slowly losing my grip on reality while worrying about you, but it’s not like I’m waking up every morning thinking about how I want to die.
: I’m just...having trouble getting to sleep. Which, all things considered, isn’t really that big of a problem compared to what some of the people I care most about are going through.
: You really worried that much?
: Does that surprise you?
: A little.
: I guess that’s fair.
I recall an earlier thought — one about my hypocrisy reigning supreme as I leave a girl to rot.
And like clockwork, it will reign supreme once more right now.
Just this time, it will be in paradoxic contradiction to itself as my hypocrisy is squared until it comes full circle.
: Have I ever helped you with anything?
: Because all this time, I’ve been telling myself that what I’ve been doing for you was what was best. But I don’t know if I ever actually believed that or if I just...made myself believe it.
: I guess what I’m asking is...do you need something different from me? Or...want something different from me?
: Should I be less of an asshole? More of an asshole?
: I’m just not sure with you.
: I think I’m normally pretty good at reading people but, for a while, it’s felt like every time I’ve tried to do that with you, I’ve come up with nothing.
: I’m obviously not...trying to take the place of your father or anything. But I think having one more person on your side is something that could really benefit you right now.
: Especially if you’re not going to let your mom be one of those people.
: Sensei...
: Have you ever lost someone you loved?
: Someone that meant the world to you?
: Does it ever get better?
: What can I do to make this all feel better?!
